dataset.description: The EU Restoration Law and the Habitats Directive are key frameworks relevant to this proposal. The EU Restoration Law, part of the European Green Deal, emphasizes the restoration of ecosystems critical to biodiversity and carbon sequestration, such as P. oceanica meadows. These meadows are recognized as essential habitats under Annex I of the Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC), which mandates member states to maintain or restore their natural habitats to a favourable conservation status. Understanding fruit dispersal pathways and potential settlement areas will enhance the success of restoration efforts and inform strategies for compliance with EU biodiversity goals. Furthermore, the outcomes of this study will contribute to the EU Mission "Restore our Ocean and Waters by 2030" by supporting evidence-based restoration techniques for degraded seagrass meadows, thus addressing both ecological and policy-driven restoration priorities.

dmp.description: This project aims to experimentally quantify the movement ecology of Posidonia oceanica fruits under controlled conditions, using a current flume to simulate realistic combinations of currents and wind observed at sea. We aim to measure fruit speeds under 10 current and 8 wind intensities and 2 wind directions to provide useful data to model dispersal distances and trajectories of fruits at sea. In addition, improved identification of beach-cast sites could facilitate seed collection efforts, making seed-based restoration techniques more practical and scalable. This approach would support the production of seedlings for transplantation, facilitating both aquaculture applications and large-scale Posidonia oceanica restoration initiatives.
